added: packages/runtime-contracts (@sos-2/runtime-contracts): the typed runtime vocabulary for runtime/execution integration — the §4 harness integration priority order (native API/SDK/app-server -> MCP/equivalent protocol -> local companion/service bridge -> browser/IDE extension -> UI automation LAST) as a frozen, typed, deterministic selection model (selectRuntimeIntegration: the highest AVAILABLE control surface wins; SOS must never require an extension when an equivalent safe API is available — pinned by tests); runtime capability envelopes (capability + operation vocabulary + candidate integration surfaces, each guarded); the bounded-environment description (filesystem scope, network egress policy, isolation level, resource limits, environment variable NAMES only — never secret values, mirroring the P3 environment-contract discipline with ZERO ambient process.env reads anywhere); and the non-semantic identifier discipline (assertValidRuntimeIdentifier rejects spine-shaped sos:// values loudly — runtime identifiers are NEVER SOS semantic identities). The P3 body-provider configuration vocabulary (@sos-2/infra-deployment) mirrors the SAME §3 surfaces as an independent vocabulary: alignment is BY SPEC, import deliberately absent (the P3 structural-isolation precedent), pinned by a structural scan test.

packages/harness (@sos-2/harness): the Harness Contract — the execution contract of spec/productization-execution-architecture.md §9 as typed interfaces, namespaced exactly as specified: identity(), capabilities(), createTask(), resumeTask(), pauseTask(), cancelTask(), workspace.read(), workspace.write(), shell.exec(), browser.open(), browser.interact(), git.status(), git.diff(), git.commit(), git.push(), git.createBranch(), git.createPullRequest(), artifacts.capture(), observations.emit(), events.subscribe(). Every operation answers a typed HarnessResult (OK/FAILURE | FAILED/FAILURE — the operation RAN and failed, truthful | UNSUPPORTED — the operation is explicitly not carried by the binding advertisement); unsupported capabilities are EXPLICIT, never silent failure. The capability advertisement model mirrors the §3 body advertisement list FIELD-FOR-FIELD (capabilities, isolationLevel, networkPolicy, filesystemScope, browser, shell, git, runtimeIntegrations, taskLifecycle, evidenceCapture, costEnvelope) with a binding advertisement map (isOperationAdvertised) and cross-consistency validation (an operation list without its surface capability is a rejected lie). The contract surface carries NO authority fields at all: a body can neither mint, carry nor widen authority; bodies are clock-less (the fabric stamps instants).

packages/body-broker (@sos-2/body-broker): the broker of the Spirit/Body architecture — body identity as a TYPED SEPARATION from SOS semantic identity (assertValidBodyId rejects spine-shaped values loudly; the provider block is provenance metadata only, never identity, never a selection key — pinned by tests); the body health lifecycle (AVAILABLE -> SUSPENDED -> AVAILABLE; AVAILABLE|SUSPENDED -> RELEASED terminal — a released body never returns); CAPABILITY-BASED body selection from declared §3 advertisements (selectBody: capability superset + placement + registration order; the selection path structurally carries no vendor fields — pinned by provider-name-flip tests); and BODY LEASES over the durable P2 BodyLeaseRepository (consumed verbatim): acquire (single-use deterministic lease ids), renew (CAS-guarded; a lease whose expiry has passed is DENIED renewal — a dead lease never reauthorizes, not even itself), release/revoke (terminal), and the FAIL-CLOSED authorization gate (authorizeLeaseOperation: lease truth recomputed from the durable record + the injected clock through live-store's isLeaseExpiredAt — consumed, never re-implemented; an expired, revoked or released lease authorizes NOTHING, typed LeaseDenial, pinned by tests). The broker may suspend, replace or release a body WITHOUT losing the task: replaceBodyLease ends the current lease (or carries an already-ended one — the kill-mid-task flow) and acquires a NEW single-use lease for the SAME task on a capability-selected replacement body; the durable TaskRecord is never touched by the broker.

packages/execution-fabric (@sos-2/execution-fabric): the provider-neutral orchestration surface composing harness + broker + the durable P2 stores + authority into bounded task execution. The uniform gate pipeline on EVERY consequential operation, in order: TASK (durable record exists and is RUNNING) -> LEASE (the fail-closed broker gate) -> AUTHORITY (the CURRENT grant heads resolve over the durable AuthorityGrantRepository — the supersedes chain is walked FORWARD so a mid-task revocation recorded as a successor revision is what gets evaluated — and re-evaluate through @sos-2/authority's evaluateGrant at the injected instant, the W12 ExecutionAdapter pattern) -> ADVERTISEMENT (the binding §3 capability advertisement must carry the operation) -> DISPATCH (the §9 contract surface). Every attempt — executed, denied or unsupported — lands in the typed OBSERVATION BOUNDARY (durable, replay-protected P2 events; deterministic sequence ids) and the task record updates through CAS-guarded writes (§6 TaskRecord shape: checkpoints, content-addressed artifacts via the P2 ObjectStoreAdapter, observations, final verification). A BODY CANNOT MINT OR WIDEN AUTHORITY: the operation surface validates exact request shapes (an injected grant/authority key is a typed OPERATION_INVALID denial naming the smuggled field), grants resolve ONLY from the durable store (a forged reference is AUTHORITY_GRANT_MISSING), the task's authority context is fixed at creation, and body outputs — including body completion reports — enter the observation boundary as NON-AUTHORITATIVE pre-semantic input: a body may report completion but may not certify mission success (§10); only the Spirit-side completeTask with the verification record completes a task (pinned by tests). Task identity is durable: replaceBodyForTask ends the current lease, acquires a new one on a capability-selected replacement body, parks a RUNNING task to PAUSED and points the SAME durable record at the new lease — kill mid-task -> new body -> resume preserves the task id and all durable state (pinned by tests).

tests/harness-contracts (@sos-2/harness-contracts): the acceptance suites — a fake/reference body (a complete in-memory §9 HarnessContract implementation: workspace, shell, simulated git, browser where advertised, artifacts, observations, cursor-based events, run-flag probes) executes a COMPLETE bounded task through the public contract surface (create -> workspace write -> shell exec -> git commit -> artifacts capture -> observations emit -> complete), plus one suite per acceptance criterion: capabilities explicit and provider-neutral (typed UNSUPPORTED for unadvertised operations; selection invariant under provider-name flips; §3 field-for-field mirror; §4 tier priority inside the advertisement), body lease expiry/revocation fails closed (typed denials + run-flag proofs + the P2 expireDue path + denied renewal of a dead lease), a body cannot mint authority (smuggled-grant typed rejection, forged-reference denial, mid-task expiry/revocation denials, forged payloads ride only as opaque observations, a body completion report never certifies), provider/vendor identity never becomes SOS semantic identity (guards both directions; fabric ids vs spine refs in the TaskRecord; vendor names only in provenance), body replacement preserves task identity (the full kill -> replace -> resume -> complete journey with a different vendor's body), and structural scans: ZERO new external dependencies (workspace:* + the existing toolchain only, checked against the base lockfile) and offline determinism (no Date.now/Math.random/fetch/process.env in the owned package sources; the repository's deterministic vitest seed).
preserved_invariants: the frozen W0-W18 core and every merged Wave-1 file remain untouched: all changes are additive under the owned paths packages/harness, packages/body-broker, packages/execution-fabric, packages/runtime-contracts and tests/harness-contracts; spec/, docs/, scripts/, .github/, pnpm-workspace.yaml and every existing packages/*, apps/*, infra/* and tests/* source are byte-identical to the base head c9baa42a72d76246a19144bf1679b8687d5a2d62

the Semantic Spine remains the ONLY identity/envelope/kind/trace/serialization authority: the P5 packages mint no spine ids, register no artifact kinds and define no trace types; spine artifact ids appear only as consumed references validated by the spine's own guards (isArtifactId), and the non-semantic identifier discipline (runtime-contracts) rejects spine-shaped values wherever harness/body/runtime identities occur — harness/provider identity is NEVER SOS semantic identity, pinned by tests in both directions

bodies cannot mint or widen authority (spec/productization-execution-architecture.md §13, spec/productization-requirements.md): the §9 contract surface carries no authority fields; the fabric's operation surface validates exact request shapes and typed-rejects injected authority keys (OPERATION_INVALID naming the smuggled field); grants resolve ONLY from the durable AuthorityGrantRepository and re-evaluate through @sos-2/authority's evaluateGrant on EVERY consequential operation (expired/revoked grants yield typed denials and the operation never runs — run-flag proofs); the task's authority context is fixed at creation; body outputs are non-authoritative observations and a body completion report never certifies a task — only the Spirit-side verification record completes (§10) — all pinned by negative tests

body lease discipline FAILS CLOSED: an expired, revoked or released lease authorizes nothing (typed LeaseDenial on every operation path; the broker gate recomputes lease truth from the durable record plus the injected clock through live-store's isLeaseExpiredAt — consumed, never re-implemented); a dead lease cannot even renew itself; lease ids are single-use and never reactivate — pinned by tests

task state is durable and body-independent (§1/§6): the task IS its durable TaskRecord — kill-mid-task -> body replacement -> resume preserves the task id, checkpoints, artifacts and observations; the broker never touches task records; the fabric's only lease-affecting transitions are explicit (cancel/complete release; replacement re-points) — pinned by tests

harnesses/bodies are replaceable execution mechanisms and providers remain adapters: capability-based body selection never consults vendor identity (structurally vendor-blind selection inputs, pinned by provider-name-flip tests); unsupported capabilities are explicit typed UNSUPPORTED results, never silent failure; the §4 integration priority order is a frozen typed model (never require an extension when an equivalent safe API is available)

unknown, failed, unavailable and unsupported remain distinct (spec/architecture.md §18 / R21): the harness result union keeps SUCCESS (ran and succeeded), FAILURE (ran and failed) and UNSUPPORTED (never dispatched) separate; fabric denials (never ran — lease/authority/shape) are recorded as denial observations distinct from executed failures; refusing-to-run and running-and-failing are never conflated

zero new external dependencies (runtime or dev): every dependency of the five new packages is a workspace:* link and every devDependency is the repository's existing toolchain (@types/node, typescript, vitest — already resolved by the base pnpm-lock.yaml for the existing suites), pinned by structural scan tests; pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml remain unchanged (git diff --stat empty on both)

determinism and offline execution: no Date.now, no Math.random, no fetch, no process.env in any owned package source — clocks, stores, broker and entropy are injected (ManualClock in tests); observation ids and lease ids are deterministic sequences; every suite runs offline with the repository's fixed vitest seed (pinned by structural scans)
